entry.content:

Tidal announced that it will ban, reject, and remove fully AI-generated music from its platform following an influx of submissions where over 43% of tracks uploaded in the prior 90 days were detected as AI-generated. Beginning December 9, the streaming service will remove over 29 million fully AI-generated songs by the end of the year and reject approximately 80,000 to 85,000 similar tracks daily.

The company will prohibit distribution services from delivering tracks made entirely by AI and will block submissions based on metadata labels, though songs featuring partial AI assistance will still be accepted. This policy escalates Tidal's earlier June 2026 decision to demonetize fully AI-generated tracks, aligning it with platforms like Bandcamp while contrasting with larger services such as Spotify and YouTube Music that primarily rely on labeling.
